quote: the benchmark Middle East Gulf-to-Far East route cost about $30,000 per day; in January freight added about $1.73 per barrel
note: Poten puts this at roughly 3 percent of delivered cost in January.

quote: just before the Iran war broke out, it was just over $200,000 a day.
as_reported_by: Associated Press via Transport Topics (Baltic Exchange TD3)
note: Rates were already high before the war on sanctions and winter demand; LSEG had the route over $170,000 a day on 24 February, a six-year high.

quote: VLCC rates from the Gulf to China initially jumped from around $4/bbl to $17/bbl
note: The same sentence gives about $4 a barrel as the pre-war rate.

quote: before easing to $11–12/bbl through April–July
note: A range for April to July; the midpoint is drawn. S&P Global via Al Jazeera put early June at a little over $60 a tonne, the low since March.

quote: On Aug. 7, the exchange assessed earnings on the Middle East-to-China route at $498,000 a day.
as_reported_by: Associated Press via Transport Topics (Baltic Exchange)
note: A record of $656,000 a day followed on 28 August.

quote: put the Middle East Gulf-to-China TD3C route at the equivalent of about $1.035m per day
note: The Signal Group has the route averaging $1.02 million a day across September, 17.5 times its 2025 average.

quote: Loaded at Ras Tanura, inside the Strait, the cargo paid about US$ 52 million in freight, or US$ 26/bbl.
as_reported_by: The Signal Group, Who Pays the Freight?
note: Kpler had $24 a barrel on 16 September; LSEG had more than $30 on 21 September.

quote: Freight now accounts for 25% of the fob crude price from the MEG and 11% from the Gulf of Oman.
note: 'up from 17% at the start of the conflict and around 5% before the war.' The nearest published series to the figure Al Jaber gave.

quote: The benchmark rate to ship crude on a VLCC to China from Saudi Arabia has surpassed $1.3 million per day
note: Bloomberg data via Oilprice had a record $1.4 million a day the same week.

quote: the cost of shipping crude from the Middle East Gulf to Asia on a large tanker had climbed to over $37 per barrel
note: 'more than five times its level before the war began.' The Signal Group has October at about $34 from Ras Tanura; the range is drawn at its midpoint.

quote: freight adds almost $33 per barrel, about 27% of delivered cost
note: Windward: 25 to 30 percent of the cost of the commodity, against 1 to 3 percent in normal conditions. Braemar via CNBC on 30 October: 20 to 30 percent of delivered cost.

quote: Before the war, the premium stood at roughly 0.25 per cent of the hull value
note: Baselines disagree: gCaptain about 0.1 percent; Lloyd's List 0.15 to 0.25 percent for seven days.

quote: By mid-March 2026, that figure had reached 2.5% of hull value per seven-day period.
note: Some stranded tankers paid up to 10 percent of hull value for a single transit. Marsh via Reuters had 1 to 1.5 percent on 6 March; Bloomberg about 5 percent on 16 March.

quote: eased to around 2% when the US and Iran signed their memorandum of understanding in June
note: gCaptain put the post-ceasefire rate at about 1 percent of hull value a voyage, $1.1 million on a $110 million VLCC.

quote: Rates can be anywhere between 3 per cent and 10 per cent on hull value
note: S&P Global via Al Jazeera on 23 July: 7.5 to 10 percent of hull value.

quote: now costs about 6% to 10% of the ship's hull value in war-risk premiums
as_reported_by: The Boston Report (citing the Financial Times of 7 October and Marsh)
note: Up to $20 million in war insurance for one supertanker voyage. The Financial Times page itself was not opened.

quote: War-risk premiums have climbed to 7–8% of hull and machinery value (roughly $9–10 million, or $4–5/bbl)
note: The only per-barrel conversion of the hull premium found apart from Goldman's $7.

quote: The rise includes an extra $7 for the war-risk premium in the Strait of Hormuz
as_reported_by: Bloomberg via Yahoo Finance UK (Goldman Sachs note)
note: Goldman's decomposition of a global average crude freight rate above $20 a barrel, up from $3 a year earlier.

quote: and $4 each for higher fuel costs and the impact of ship-to-ship transfers.
as_reported_by: Bloomberg via Yahoo Finance UK (Goldman Sachs note)
note: Ship-to-ship transfers, $4 a barrel.

quote: and $4 each for higher fuel costs and the impact of ship-to-ship transfers.
as_reported_by: Bloomberg via Yahoo Finance UK (Goldman Sachs note)
note: Bunker fuel, $4 a barrel.

quote: This translates to about $21 in transportation costs per barrel of crude oil compared with $6.50 a barrel in September.
note: The Gulf of Oman to Asia leg alone: a supertanker for that run cost $249,000 a day in early September and more than $900,000 a day by the first week of October. Not added to the stack, since it overlaps the freight layer.

quote: National oil companies are paying tankers $50 million per transit to ship crude to ship-to-ship transfer areas off Fujairah
note: A Wall Street Journal account via Seoul Economic Daily: each shuttle run $30 to $40 million, about $15 to $20 a barrel before insurance.

quote: Demurrage rates for cargoes moving out of the Gulf have soared to $1 million/day
note: No pre-war figure found.

quote: The November OSP for Saudi Aramco's flagship Arab Light grade has been set at a $5/bbl discount to Oman/Dubai
note: The seller cutting the price of the oil to carry the freight: who pays the logistics bill.

quote: TotalEnergies was buying Gulf crude at some USD 50-60 / bbl while Brent traded above USD 90 / bbl, Pouyanne said.
note: The one buyer who said what he paid: a discounted price at the Gulf, and about $20 million to move a shipment through the strait.

quote: Shipping and logistics costs, which accounted for less than 5 per cent of the cost of a barrel before the disruption, now exceed 30 per cent.
as_reported_by: The National (reporting Sultan Al Jaber, ADNOC, at ADIPEC)
note: No basis given in any of the four reports of the speech. The page checks it against the sum of the sourced layers.

quote: Iranian Light into China has flipped from a steep $12/bbl discount to a $1/bbl premium to ICE Brent
note: The pre-war discount, not dated to a month by the source; drawn at February.

quote: Iranian crude, once deeply discounted, is now trading at a $1/bbl premium to ICE Brent
note: A premium: with the strait shut to everyone else, the barrel that could still move was worth more. Reuters trade sources had premiums of $1 to $2 in April and May.

quote: Iranian Light crude is being offered at a discount of 50 cents to $1 per barrel against ICE Brent for delivery this month
as_reported_by: Iran International (citing three traders who spoke to Reuters)

quote: Iranian Light for delivery in September was offered at discounts of about $4 a barrel to ICE Brent earlier this month
note: Narrowed from about $5. Kpler: close to 30 million barrels of Iranian crude on tankers in Asian waters.

quote: Iranian crude and condensate exports trended at roughly 1.7 Mbd prior to the war
note: Oilprice, unattributed satellite tracking: 2.2 million a day loaded in February, 1.9 in March.

quote: fell to near zero in May and the first half of June following the US naval blockade imposed in mid-April.
note: Near zero, drawn as empty.

quote: Iranian crude loadings fell to around 210kbd in August, down from roughly 2mbd earlier this year
note: Iran suspended a 10 percent freight charge on foreign vessels carrying its oil the same month.

quote: Iranian oil stored aboard tankers in Asian waters had been depleted by mid-October
as_reported_by: International Business Times via Yahoo (citing the Wall Street Journal and Kpler)
note: Floating stock down from about 90 million barrels in mid-July to about 29 million. Reuters in September: no Iranian crude cargo had crossed the strait toward China since the blockade resumed on 14 July. No October differential was quoted anywhere: there was nothing to price.

quote: as exports have increased by 30%, from 3.9 million barrels per day in February to 5.2 million barrels per day in April
note: The EIA's own monthly series, drawn on the page, has February 4.3 and April 5.6.

quote: combined adjusted net income of $56.3 billion in the most recent quarter
note: ExxonMobil, Chevron, BP, Shell and TotalEnergies together, third quarter 2026. ExxonMobil's refining division earned a record $9.05 billion; Chevron's refineries $4.93 billion. No source puts a per-barrel figure on what American producers gained.
